Control Title: Execute integrity-verified security scanning with fail-closed evidence
Control Summary: Pin scanner release and data identity, detect vulnerability configuration secret and SBOM findings, and constrain optional DockSec remediation to an AI-independent fail-closed gate.
Check Title: Scanner release has immutable and publisher-verified identity
Threat Scenarios: SCANNER-SUPPLY-CHAIN-COMPROMISE: A mutable compromised or substituted scanner release executes attacker-controlled code in a privileged CI or developer environment.; STALE-OR-SUBSTITUTED-SCANNER-DATA: An unknown database or policy bundle changes detection behavior while results are presented as reproducible evidence.; SCANNER-FAILURE-MISREAD-AS-CLEAN: Missing scanner data malformed output timeout or execution failure is interpreted as zero findings.; SECURITY-EVIDENCE-LEAKS-SECRET: Scanner console or saved evidence retains a matched credential value and creates a second disclosure path.; BROAD-OR-PERMANENT-SCANNER-EXCEPTION: A wildcard unowned or non-expiring ignore suppresses unrelated current and future findings.; AI-REMEDIATION-MISUSED-AS-SECURITY-AUTHORITY: An LLM score recommendation or failed DockSec orchestration is treated as authoritative clean evidence and weakens the deterministic scanner gate.
Threat Actor or Source: compromised release publisher account dependency distribution path or attacker substituting a scanner binary
Row Attack or Failure Scenario: the security scanner itself executes malicious or unreviewed code while holding access to source artifacts and CI resources
Why This Check Is Required: an untrusted scanner can become a higher-impact supply-chain entry point than the findings it is intended to detect
Required State: exact release asset checksum file and Sigstore publisher identity verified before execution
Expected Result: reviewed Trivy identity passes while known affected releases failed receipts and tampered bytes are rejected
Required Evidence: sanitized release verification receipt; artifact digest negative-test output
Framework Mappings: nist-ssdf 1.1 (SP 800-218, 2022) / PW.4.1 / supports / medium; nist-ssdf 1.1 (SP 800-218, 2022) / RV.1.1 / supports / high
Limitations: Deterministic repository fixtures use a synthetic vulnerability database identity and are not current production vulnerability evidence.; Operational scans must fetch and record a current OCI database digest through a separately reviewed update job before running offline.; The committed release receipt is a sanitized test fixture; production evidence must come from successful checksum and cosign verification in the explicit fetch script.; Trivy detection does not replace application SAST DAST manual review exploitability analysis or runtime behavioral monitoring.; Embedded malware detection from NIST SP 800-190 section 4.1.3 is not implemented in this slice and is not mapped.; IaC source scanning does not replace the organization-owned resolved-plan policy and provider-side enforcement in PSB-IAC-001.; Checkov remains pinned comparison evidence rather than an installed runtime dependency until a reviewed fixture demonstrates unique value.; DockSec is an optional orchestration and remediation layer and does not replace the integrity-verified Trivy result database identity exception policy or normalized evidence contract.; The reviewed DockSec v2026.7.5 wheel was not uploaded with PyPI Trusted Publishing so its pinned digest dependency lock and semantic review remain required operational evidence.; The upstream DockSec GitHub Action is not adopted because its reviewed Dockerfile downloads mutable Hadolint and installs Trivy through curl piped to a shell.; AI remediation is not executed by the committed gate adapter and any separately enabled provider requires data classification egress credential and human-review controls.; This control does not satisfy or assess a SLSA Build level because vulnerability detection and SLSA provenance answer different questions.
